w: Explain equal triangle areas using common base 12 cm and equal perpendicular altitudes 7 cm despite different apex offsets; compute 42 cm² each.

rubric.criterion: Correctly identifies the same 12 cm base for both triangles
Recognizes perpendicular 7 cm altitude to the base line, not the slanted side
Uses A=bh/2 or a mathematically equivalent independent area proof as the equality warrant
Computes both areas as 42 cm² with square units
Does not misinterpret sideways apex offset as changing perpendicular height

review_instructions: A qualified reviewer must compare the learner's actual justification with the conceptual rubric; sample tokens, phrase similarity, numerical-only matching and nonblank-attempt gating are not automatic academic grading. Allow mathematically equivalent proofs and meaningful partial-credit distinctions. Sample probes are illustrative, never an exhaustive classifier.

cases.response: Both triangles use base AB = 12 cm. The 7 cm distances are perpendicular heights, so the triangle area formula gives (12 × 7)/2 = 42 cm² for each. Horizontal position of the peaks does not change these values.
cases.proposed_human_feedback_after_commit: Confirm the relation A=bh/2 and why it applies separately to both shapes.

cases.response: Place A=(0,0), B=(12,0), C=(2,7), D=(10,7). The absolute determinant area for both ABC and ABD is |12×7|/2=42 square cm, so the areas match.
cases.proposed_human_feedback_after_commit: Equivalent proof by determinant is mathematically valid even if the formula is shown through coordinates.

cases.response: Moving the apex sideways keeps its distance at right angles to AB at 7 cm. Each has the same 12 cm baseline, and area is half base times height; both are 42 cm².
cases.proposed_human_feedback_after_commit: Accept geometric shear/invariance phrasing that states the base-height warrant.
Ask why both figures have the same area; a number alone does not establish the warrant.

cases.response: Yes, the areas are the same.
cases.proposed_human_feedback_after_commit: Ask for matched base and perpendicular height, the governing relation, and both areas.

cases.response: Yes, because the two triangles look almost the same.
cases.proposed_human_feedback_after_commit: Visual resemblance is neither a sufficient criterion nor a proof; compare base and right-angle height.

cases.response: They have the same base, so every triangle on that base has identical area.
cases.proposed_human_feedback_after_commit: Challenge with a shared 8 cm base and altitudes 5 and 4 cm; areas differ.

cases.response: Both have a side going up 7 cm, so treat the slanted side as the height.
cases.proposed_human_feedback_after_commit: Only a 90-degree distance to the chosen base line qualifies as altitude.

cases.response: No. C and D are in different sideways locations, so their triangle areas must differ.
cases.proposed_human_feedback_after_commit: Horizontal shifts do not change b or perpendicular h.

cases.response: Both are equal because a triangle has area 12 + 7 = 19 square cm.
cases.proposed_human_feedback_after_commit: Area is half the product of base and perpendicular altitude, not their sum.

cases.response: Both heights are 7 and base is 12, so area is 84 cm² each.
cases.proposed_human_feedback_after_commit: The direction of the equality argument may be correct; divide the base-height product by two.

cases.response: Both use A=12×7/2 and so each area is 42 cm.
cases.proposed_human_feedback_after_commit: Area units are square centimetres, not centimetres.

cases.response: If the perpendicular foot lies beyond the segment AB, you cannot measure a triangle height, so equal area cannot be justified.
cases.proposed_human_feedback_after_commit: The altitude is measured to the infinite straight line through the base, extended if necessary.

cases.response: For both triangles with area 36 cm² and base 12 cm, the height must be 36÷12=3 cm.
cases.proposed_human_feedback_after_commit: The converse relation uses h=2A/b, so each perpendicular height is 6 cm.

cases.response: For each triangle A=bh/2. With A=36 cm² and positive b=12 cm, h=2×36/12=6 cm for both.
The shared base of 8 cm does not guarantee equal areas if heights are 5 and 4 cm: their areas are 20 and 16 cm².
cases.proposed_human_feedback_after_commit: Valid falsifying boundary for an overgeneralized common-base claim.
